title: CW1-CL: three-qubit leaves with strided backward recovery

claims.statement: For every integer N>=2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single CW1-CL algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, including its finite branch, fallback predicate, source cap, and per-bit attempt caps, recovers the complete s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failures, wrong labels and aborts, its total charged sequential work obeys T(N,s)=O(n^(7/2) (log2 n) 2^((3/2)sqrt(n))). The full uniform bit-length envelope is B_T(n)=n^(7/2) (log2 n) 2^((3/2)sqrt(n)) for n>=2, with the explicit finite branch covering n=1. Its exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes. This bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N>=2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single CW1-CL algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, including its finite branch, fallback predicate, source cap, and per-bit attempt caps, recovers the complete s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failures, wrong labels and aborts, its peak classical bits obeys S_C(N,s)=O(n^2 2^(sqrt(n))). The full uniform bit-length envelope is B_S_C(n)=n^2 2^(sqrt(n)) for n>=2, with the explicit finite branch covering n=1. Its exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes. This bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N>=2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single CW1-CL algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, including its finite branch, fallback predicate, source cap, and per-bit attempt caps, recovers the complete s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failures, wrong labels and aborts, its peak qubits obeys S_Q(N,s)=O(n). The full uniform bit-length envelope is B_S_Q(n)=n for n>=2, with the explicit finite branch covering n=1. Its exact growth index is 0/1. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes. This bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N>=2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n=ceil(log2 N), the single CW1-CL algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, including its finite branch, fallback predicate, source cap, and per-bit attempt caps, recovers the complete s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failures, wrong labels and aborts, its total acquired source copies, including all rejected and discarded copies obeys Q(N,s)=O(n 2^((3/2)sqrt(n))). The full uniform bit-length envelope is B_Q(n)=n 2^((3/2)sqrt(n)) for n>=2, with the explicit finite branch covering n=1. Its exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes. This bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For the same CW1-CL algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, the proved malformed-sample fractional guarantee is epsilon(n)=0: every acquired copy is an independent ideal coset state. Under this promise, for every N>=2 and every s, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
